subject: Invoice sequencing & VAT treatment — clarification on order form redline
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam@acme-corp.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Cc: billing@acme-corp.com
Date: Mon, 08 Sep 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Draft order form redline — invoice sequencing & VAT question

Jonas —

Thanks for taking a look. Attached is our second pass on the order form with a few commercial asks from procurement:
- We want invoicing on a monthly cadence but need the invoices aligned to feature-release milestones (so amounts will vary per invoice).
- VAT: Acme is VAT-registered in Ireland; procurement expects Redwood to invoice with VAT applied to the invoice recipient entity unless Redwood confirms reverse-charge acceptance.
- Net terms: our procurement team prefers net-60; accounting is pushing net-45. Please confirm Redwood's stance — we typically accept net-60 for enterprise pilots.
- Can you confirm the invoice payee entity? We have multiple entities and need the invoice routed to Acme Holdings Ltd (EU entity) for our AP workflow.

We're attaching the redline for the Order Form (Acme_OrderForm_Redline_v2.docx). If possible, can you provide a short commercial summary showing how the minimum commit will be invoiced across the first three months? That will help our CFO sign off.

Appreciate a quick turnaround this week — procurement wants to circulate a final to legal by Friday.

Best,
Liam O'Connor
Procurement Manager
Acme Corp

Attachments: Acme_OrderForm_Redline_v2.docx (docx, 42KB)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>, billing@acme-corp.com
Date: Mon, 08 Sep 2025 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft order form redline — invoice sequencing & VAT question

Liam —

Thanks for the redline and the clear asks. Quick answers up front, then a short plan:

1) Invoicing cadence / sequencing
- We can support monthly invoicing tied to milestones. To keep accounting straightforward, we propose a single invoice per month with line items mapped to the milestone(s) completed in that window.
- For the minimum commit, we’ll split the up-front portion pro rata across the first three monthly invoices unless you prefer a single upfront charge.

2) VAT treatment
- Redwood's default is to apply VAT when invoicing an EU-registered entity unless the customer confirms reverse-charge applicability and provides a valid VAT registration number.
- If Acme provides the EU VAT number for Acme Holdings Ltd and confirms reverse-charge is the desired approach, we'll update the order form language and invoice accordingly.

3) Net terms
- Standard hosted pilot terms we offer are net-45; net-60 is possible but needs Finance approval (we evaluate on a deal-by-deal basis).
- For this deal we can provisionally accept net-60 if Acme signs the payment milestone schedule and provides the PO up front. Final approval by Finance expected within 48 hours.

4) Invoice payee entity
- We need the legal entity name, VAT number (if applicable), and PO number to lock the invoice recipient.

Next steps proposed:
- I’ll attach a brief commercial summary that shows the three-month distribution of the minimum commit and the monthly invoicing example. (See attached Jonas_Response_notes.pdf).
- Kimberly, can you review the redline for legal/Tax language changes around reverse-charge and make any edits to the order form?

Liam — if you can confirm the PO number and VAT id for Acme Holdings Ltd by EOD Thursday we should be able to get to a countersigned Order Form and DocuSign this week.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Head of Sales — EMEA
Redwood Inference
jonas@redwood.com | +44 20 5555 1234

Attachments: Jonas_Response_notes.pdf (pdf, 18KB)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Liam O'Connor <liam@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 09 Sep 2025 09:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft order form redline — invoice sequencing & VAT question

Jonas / Liam —

I reviewed the order form redline and left a few targeted comments in the attached PDF (OrderForm_Legal_Redline.pdf). High-level items:

- VAT / Reverse-charge: we can accept reverse-charge for EU customers where supported, but we need Acme's VAT registration number in writing and a written confirmation that Acme will self-account under local law. I added a short clause to 2.1 clarifying invoicing treatment and requested the VAT id in the definitions table.

- Net terms: our preferred commercial is net-45. If Acme requires net-60, we need an explicit payment milestone (e.g., PO issuance + first invoice due in 60 days) and a Finance escalation approval. Please confirm whether Acme will provide a PO that references the Order Form and the required milestone schedule.

- Invoice recipient entity: legal asked to include an invoice recipient appendix to avoid cross-entity ambiguity. The appendix requires: (i) legal name, (ii) registered address, (iii) VAT id, (iv) AP contact and email, (v) PO number.

- Service credits / SLA: small ask — we added a 10% withholding remedy clause if invoices are disputed beyond 60 days to protect Redwood in case of delayed payment. This is limited and only kicks in after our standard dispute process completes.

- DocuSign: I've prepared the redline and am happy to produce a final clean version for countersignature once the commercial points above are confirmed. Sending the OrderForm_Legal_Redline.pdf as requested.

Naomi — I tagged a couple of commercial fallback options in the comments (prepay vs staged invoice) — can you surface those in the commercial summary back to Acme so procurement has a clear ask to their CFO?

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel — Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference
kimberly@redwood.com

Attachments: OrderForm_Legal_Redline.pdf (pdf, 24KB)
